//name: PERMANENT. Raycast keys this extension's encrypted LocalStorage by (name, author), so changing either after the first publish orphans every install's stored credential, its durable queue of unsent writes and its cross-process state echo — with no error anywhere. See PUBLISHING.md. Written once from the project's identifier set by `hatchkit`; never re-derived.
name: starter-launcher
title: Starter Launcher
description: Capture and review your items from the launcher, with the work you do offline queued until the server answers again.
//author: The other half of the storage key, and the store listing's identity. The value here is a scaffold placeholder so `ray develop` runs; the real store handle is a decision passed to `scripts/export-store.mjs --author`, and only the exported copy is ever published.
author: starter-author

commands.name: current-item
commands.title: Current Item
commands.subtitle: Starter Launcher
commands.description: Show the item you touched last, kept fresh while the window is open.
commands.//interval: Raycast unloads a menu bar command once its first render settles, so the timer inside it fires once. This declared interval is what covers the unloaded case; the surface's own unfinished-load state covers the loaded one.

preferences.name: showPending
preferences.title: Menu Bar
preferences.label: Show unsent work in the title
preferences.description: Add the number of changes still waiting to be sent to the menu bar title.

commands.name: capture-item
commands.title: Capture Item
commands.description: Create an item without opening a window. Bind a global hotkey to this one.
commands.//mode: `no-view` is the reason this command exists. A global hotkey can only drive a background-capable mode, and a view command opens a window before it can do anything — so folding this into the form command silently costs the hotkey.

preferences.title: After Capturing
preferences.label: Open the web app
preferences.description: Open the new item in the web app once the server has confirmed it.

commands.description: Fill in an item and send it, or queue it when there is no answer.

//preferences: Neither origin carries a `default`. Raycast stores a manifest default as a real preference value, which makes "never touched it" indistinguishable from "deliberately typed the production origin" — and the build-mode fallback in src/lib/preferences.ts could then never fire.

preferences.name: apiOrigin
preferences.title: API Origin
preferences.description: Where the API lives, e.g. https://example.com. Leave empty to use the origin this build was made for.

preferences.name: webOrigin
preferences.title: Web App Origin
preferences.description: Where the web app lives. Leave empty to use the origin this build was made for.

//dependencies: zod is not imported by src/ directly. It is a runtime dependency of the VENDORED offline overlay (src/vendor/offline-overlay.ts), and `node scripts/vendor-core.mjs --check` fails when a vendored file imports a package this manifest does not declare — the store's build machine would otherwise be the first place that fails. Note the placement: a `//`-prefixed key is inert at the TOP level of a manifest and is read as a PACKAGE NAME inside `dependencies`, where it breaks the install.

scripts.//scripts: The store copy does NOT get these. scripts/export-store.mjs replaces the whole block with Raycast's own template scripts, because `pnpm`, the vendor step and the export itself do not exist outside this repository.
scripts.build: pnpm run vendor && ray build -e dist -o dist
scripts.//lint: eslint + prettier directly, NOT `ray lint`. The root `lint` script is `pnpm -r --if-present run lint`, so whatever is here runs in CI — and `ray lint` always validates the manifest's `author` against the store's HTTP API, which fails for the scaffold placeholder and makes a network call CI has no business making. The manifest schema, the icon and the author handle are checked by `lint:store` instead, which is a pre-submission step.
scripts.//lint:store: The pre-submission check: the manifest schema, the icon, the metadata and the author handle. It needs the network and cannot pass with the scaffold's placeholder handle, so it is not in the repository's `lint` aggregate. See PUBLISHING.md.
scripts.//publish: A guard, not a publish. Publishing happens only from the exported copy — see PUBLISHING.md — because the in-repo manifest carries scaffold placeholders for the two permanent fields.
